answer: Shared-secret bridge attestation. Each identity receives a private jade token when joining, and every transaction must include a crystal hash derived from that token plus the counterparty's identity. Duplicates produce identical hashes only when interacting with the same counterparty, exposing the fork; honest agents rotate salts per pair. An attacker duplicating N identities must maintain N distinct token histories across all counterparties, costing one unique attested interaction per identity per epoch plus detection risk from any repeated hash pair.
